A recent social media post claims that Israel “dropped MOMO, the international excess mortality registry website, after 8 weeks of worse results than 2020 despite vaccination,” asserting that this is proof mortality rises with the vaccine. This claim has gained traction online, reflecting ongoing debates about COVID-19 vaccination and its impact on public health data. To assess its accuracy, it is important to unpack the central elements: Israel’s use of the so-called MOMO registry, excess mortality data in Israel, and the relationship between vaccination and mortality.

First, it is necessary to clarify what MOMO refers to in this context. The European Mortality Monitoring Project (EuroMOMO) is a collaborative network that monitors weekly excess mortality across several European countries. Its data are publicly available and widely used to track the impact of COVID-19 and other health events. Israel was included in EuroMOMO’s reporting for a period during the pandemic, contributing national mortality figures for comparison.

The social media post suggests that Israel’s withdrawal from the registry was motivated by “worse results than 2020,” which refers to higher excess mortality despite the country’s early and robust vaccine rollout. In early 2021, Israel became one of the first countries to rapidly vaccinate a large proportion of its population against COVID-19, leading international observers to closely monitor its public health outcomes.

Examining the claim that Israel experienced eight consecutive weeks of excess mortality worse than 2020, it is true that several countries, including Israel, saw spikes in deaths during waves of COVID-19 variants. However, excess mortality is influenced by many factors: COVID-19 case surges, new variants, delayed medical care, and social disruptions. The assertion that these figures directly result from vaccination oversimplifies a complex situation.

The post further claims that Israel dropped MOMO specifically to hide negative results. In reality, countries periodically change their participation in international registries for various reasons, including methodological updates, resource constraints, or shifts in national data reporting. There is no official evidence that Israel withdrew from EuroMOMO due to inconvenient mortality data or as an attempt to obscure the impact of vaccines. Data on Israeli mortality continues to be published by its official statistical agencies and is accessible for independent analysis.

Finally, the core claim—“proof that mortality rises with the vaccine”—lacks substantiation. Extensive studies worldwide show that COVID-19 vaccines significantly reduce severe illness and death from the virus. While some periods of excess mortality have coincided with vaccination campaigns, these usually correspond to surges in COVID-19 itself or other confounding factors, not the vaccines. Surveillance systems in Israel and elsewhere have not found evidence of widespread increases in all-cause mortality attributable to vaccination.

In summary, the social media post misrepresents Israel’s relationship with the EuroMOMO registry and draws unsupported conclusions about vaccines and mortality. While excess mortality remains a critical metric for pandemic assessment, attributing its fluctuations solely to vaccination disregards the broader epidemiological context and the overwhelming evidence of vaccine safety and effectiveness.

Evropski projekt praćenja smrtnosti (EuroMOMO) je zajednički mrežni projekt koji praćenje nedeljnih prekomernih smrtnih slučajeva u više evropskih zemalja. Podaci su javno dostupni i široko korišćeni za praćenje uticaja kovida-19 i drugih zdravstvenih događaja. Izrael je bio uključen u izveštavanje EuroMOMO tokom pandemije, doprinoseći nacionalnim podacima o smrtnosti za usporedbu.

Društveni mrežni post predlaže da je Izrael izostao iz registra zato što "rezultati su bili lošiji od 2020. godine," što se odnosi na veću prekomernu smrtnost iako je zemlja jedna od prvih da brzo vakcinise veliki deo svog stanovništva protiv kovida-19. U ranom 2021. godini, Izrael je postao jedan od prvih zemalja da brzo vakcinise veliki deo svog stanovništva protiv kovida-19, što je dovelo međunarodnih posmatrača da pažljivo praćeno njegove javno zdravstvene rezultate.

Ispitivanje tvrdnje da je Izrael imao osam uzastopnih nedelja prekomernog smrtnog rata lošijeg od 2020. godine, tačno je da su neke zemlje, uključujući Izrael, videli poraste smrtnosti tokom valova kovida-19 varijanti. Međutim, prekomerni smrtni slučajevi zavise od mnogih faktora: porast slučajeva kovida-19, novih varijanti, odlaganja medicinske pomoći i društvenih poremećaja. Tvrdnja da su ovi podaci direktno rezultat vakcinacije jednostavno pojednostavljuje kompleksnu situaciju.

Post dalje tvrdi da je Izrael izostao od MOMO specifično da bi skriven negativne rezultate. U stvarnosti, zemlje redovno menjaju svoju učestvovanje u međunarodnim registrima za razne razloge, uključujući metodološke ažuriranja, ograničenja resursa ili promene u nacionalnim podacima o izveštavanju. Nema službenih dokaza da je Izrael izostao iz EuroMOMO zato što su podaci o smrtnosti bili neugodni ili kao pokušaj da skrivi uticaj vakcina. Podaci o smrtnosti u Izraelu nastavljaju da se objavljuju putem službenih statističkih agencija i dostupni za nezavisnu analizu.

Na kraju, osnovna tvrdnja – „dokaz da smrtnost raste uz vakcinaciju“ – nema osnove. Išta široko istraživanje pokazuje da vakcine protiv kovida-19 značajno smanjuju ozbiljne bolesti i smrtnost od virusa. Iako su neki periodi prekomernog smrtnog rata pala u vreme vakcinacionih kampanja, obično se podudaraju sa porastima kovida-19 samim ili drugim faktorima koji smetaju, a ne vakcinacijom. Nadzorni sistemi u Izraelu i drugde nisu pronašli dokaze o širokom porastu smrtnosti od svih uzroka koji bi bili povezani sa vakcinacijom.

U završetku, društveni mrežni post netačno predstavlja odnos Izraela sa registrom EuroMOMO i izvodi neosnovane zaključke o vakcinaciji i smrtnosti. Iako prekomerni smrtni slučajevi ostaju ključan merilac za ocenu pandemije, pripisivanje njihovih fluktuacija samo vakcinaciji zanemaruje šire epidemiološke kontekst i pretežno dokaze o sigurnosti i efikasnosti vakcina.

Recently, a social media post has circulated claiming, “Vaccinated people cannot donate blood, because the vaccine completely destroys their natural antibodies.” This claim has generated concern and confusion among the public, especially those who have received COVID-19 vaccines or are considering blood donation. To assess the accuracy of this statement, it is important to examine current scientific understanding and blood donation guidelines.

Understanding Vaccines and Antibodies

Vaccines, including those for COVID-19, are designed to train the immune system to recognize and respond to specific pathogens. When a person receives a vaccine, their immune system produces antibodies against the virus or bacteria targeted by the vaccine. These antibodies, along with other components of the immune response, help protect the individual from future infections.

Contrary to the claim, vaccines do not “destroy” natural antibodies. Instead, they stimulate the production of new antibodies specifically tailored to fight the targeted disease. The immune system continues to function normally, producing a range of antibodies to protect against various pathogens, both those encountered naturally and through vaccination.

Blood Donation Guidelines

Blood donation organizations, such as national Red Cross societies and blood banks, have updated their guidelines in response to the COVID-19 pandemic and vaccination rollouts. The consensus among these organizations is that receiving a COVID-19 vaccine does not disqualify an individual from donating blood.

Typically, individuals are eligible to donate blood after receiving a vaccine if they feel well and are free of fever or significant side effects. Some organizations may recommend waiting for a short period—usually a day or two—after vaccination, primarily to ensure the donor is feeling healthy. This precaution is not due to any risk associated with vaccine-induced antibodies, but rather to avoid confusing vaccine side effects with other health issues in donors.

Debunking the Claim

The assertion that vaccinated individuals “cannot donate blood” is false. Blood donation centers actively encourage all eligible individuals—including those who are vaccinated—to donate, as the need for blood is constant. There is no evidence that vaccines, including mRNA and viral vector COVID-19 vaccines, destroy natural antibodies or compromise the safety or quality of donated blood.

Additionally, blood from vaccinated donors does not pose a risk to transfusion recipients. The antibodies present in donated blood, whether resulting from natural infection or vaccination, do not harm recipients. In some cases, the presence of certain antibodies can even be beneficial.

Conclusion

The claim that vaccinated people cannot donate blood because vaccines destroy their natural antibodies is not supported by scientific evidence or current blood donation policies. Vaccines are designed to enhance immune protection, not diminish it, and vaccinated individuals remain eligible and encouraged to donate blood, provided they meet standard health requirements. Spreading misinformation about blood donation and vaccines can undermine public health efforts and reduce the critical supply of donated blood. It is important to rely on credible sources for information regarding vaccines and blood donation.

Klaim ini telah menyebabkan kebimbangan dan kekaburan di kalangan masyarakat, terutamanya mereka yang telah menerima vaksin COVID-19 atau sedang mempertimbangkan untuk mendonorkan darah. Untuk menilai keakuratan pernyataan ini, penting untuk mengkaji pemahaman saintifik semasa dan panduan mendonorkan darah.

Memahami Vaksin dan Antibodi

Vaksin, termasuk vaksin untuk COVID-19, dirancang untuk melatih sistem imun untuk mengenali dan merespon patogen tertentu. Apabila seseorang menerima vaksin, sistem imun mereka menghasilkan antibodi terhadap virus atau bakteria yang ditargetkan oleh vaksin. Antibodi ini, bersama komponen lain dalam respons imun, membantu melindungi individu daripada infeksi masa depan.

Bersesuaian dengan klaim tersebut, vaksin tidak "menghancurkan" antibodi semulajadi. Sebaliknya, ia merangsang penghasilan antibodi baru yang disesuaikan untuk melawan penyakit yang ditargetkan. Sistem imun terus berfungsi secara normal, menghasilkan pelbagai antibodi untuk melindungi daripada patogen-patogen, sama ada yang ditemui secara semula jadi atau melalui pengurusan vaksin.

Panduan Mendonorkan Darah

Pihak-pihak yang menguruskan pengumpulan darah, seperti persatuan Merah Bumi nasional dan bank darah, telah memperbarui panduan mereka sebagai jawapan kepada pandemik COVID-19 dan pelaksanaan vaksinasi. Konsensus antara pihak-pihak ini ialah bahawa menerima vaksin COVID-19 tidak menyebabkan seseorang tidak layak untuk mendonorkan darah.

Secara umum, individu layak untuk mendonorkan darah selepas menerima vaksin jika mereka berasa sihat dan tidak mengalami demam atau kesan sampingan yang signifikan. Beberapa pihak mungkin menyarankan untuk menunggu tempoh singkat—biasanya satu atau dua hari—setelah pemberian vaksin, utamanya untuk memastikan pemberi darah berasa sihat. Precausi ini bukan disebabkan oleh sebarang risiko berkaitan dengan antibodi yang dihasilkan oleh vaksin, tetapi lebih kepada mengelakkan kesan sampingan vaksin dikacaukan dengan masalah kesihatan lain pada pemberi darah.

Membongkar Klaim

Pernyataan yang menyatakan bahawa individu yang telah disuntik vaksin "tidak boleh mendonorkan darah" adalah palsu. Pusat pemberian darah aktif menasihati semua individu yang layak—termasuk mereka yang telah disuntik vaksin—untuk mendonorkan darah, kerana keperluan darah adalah kekal. Tiada bukti yang menunjukkan bahawa vaksin, termasuk vaksin mRNA dan vaksin vektor virus COVID-19, menghancurkan antibodi semulajadi atau mengurangkan keselamatan atau kualiti darah yang didonorkan.

Selain itu, darah daripada pemberi darah yang telah disuntik tidak membahayakan penerima transfusi. Antibodi yang hadir dalam darah yang didonorkan, sama ada hasil daripada infeksi semula jadi atau vaksinasi, tidak merugikan penerima. Dalam beberapa kes, kehadiran antibodi tertentu dapat memberi manfaat.

Kesimpulan

Klaim bahawa orang yang telah disuntik vaksin tidak boleh mendonorkan darah kerana vaksin menghancurkan antibodi semulajadi mereka tidak didukung oleh bukti saintifik atau kebijakan pengumpulan darah semasa. Vaksin dirancang untuk meningkatkan perlindungan imun, bukan mengurangkannya, dan individu yang telah disuntik tetap layak serta dianjurkan untuk mendonorkan darah, selagi memenuhi keperluan kesihatan standard. Menyebar informasi palsu berkaitan pemberian darah dan vaksin boleh meruntuhkan usaha kesihatan awam dan mengurangkan bekalan darah yang kritikal. Kennedy Jr., and Dolores Cahill regarding measures taken during the COVID-19 pandemic. The post suggests that these prominent figures are pursuing legal action at Canada’s highest court related to pandemic policies, and that the court has agreed to hear the case.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to clarify the roles of the individuals mentioned, the function of the Supreme Court of Canada, and the process through which cases are accepted.

Dr. Reiner Fuellmich is a German lawyer known for his vocal opposition to pandemic-related restrictions and for promoting legal actions against public health measures internationally. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., an American environmental attorney, is also known for his opposition to certain public health policies and has become a prominent figure in the vaccine skepticism movement. Dolores Cahill is an Irish scientist who has similarly voiced strong opposition to COVID-19 policies. Although all three have been involved in various legal and advocacy efforts against pandemic measures, there is no public record of them filing a joint lawsuit in Canada.

The Supreme Court of Canada functions as the country’s highest appellate court. It does not conduct trials, nor does it hear cases of crimes against humanity in the way that international tribunals, such as the International Criminal Court, do. Instead, it reviews decisions made by lower courts and only accepts cases of national significance or those that present important questions of law. For any case to reach the Supreme Court, it must first be adjudicated in lower courts within the Canadian legal system. The Supreme Court then decides whether to grant leave to appeal, a process that is publicly documented and highly selective.

A review of the Supreme Court of Canada’s docket and public records reveals no evidence that a crimes against humanity case related to pandemic measures, brought by Dr. Fuellmich, Mr. Kennedy, or Dr. Cahill, has been accepted or is under consideration. No announcements or legal filings corroborate the claim that such an action has been initiated, let alone accepted, by the court. Furthermore, none of the individuals mentioned are members of the Canadian legal profession or residents of Canada, making it highly unlikely they would be direct litigants in a Canadian court case.

Additionally, the notion of “crimes against humanity” is a legal term with a specific definition under international law, typically prosecuted in international courts, not domestic supreme courts. The Canadian legal system does allow for the prosecution of certain international crimes, but such cases would originate in lower courts and involve Canadian authorities.

Kennedy Jr., and Dolores Cahill for actions taken during the pandemic is not supported by any available evidence. This claim appears to be false.

A recent social media post has gone viral, claiming that pharmaceutical giant Pfizer has announced an updated COVID-19 vaccine that now includes a Microsoft chip purportedly designed to reduce symptoms. This post has generated widespread discussion and concern online, prompting many to question the accuracy of the claim and its implications for public health and privacy.

To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to first consider the background of both Pfizer’s vaccine development and the persistent conspiracy theories that have surrounded COVID-19 vaccines since their introduction. Pfizer, in partnership with BioNTech, was among the first companies to develop a COVID-19 vaccine using mRNA technology. Since its initial release, Pfizer has regularly updated its vaccine formulations to address emerging variants of the virus, improve efficacy, and respond to evolving public health needs.

However, since the beginning of the COVID-19 vaccination campaign, there have been unsubstantiated conspiracy theories suggesting that the vaccines contain microchips or tracking devices, often linking technology companies such as Microsoft to these claims. These theories have been widely debunked by health authorities and independent experts, who confirm that the vaccines contain only the ingredients listed in their public documentation, none of which include microchips or electronic components.

The claim that Pfizer’s updated COVID-19 vaccine “now includes a Microsoft chip to reduce symptoms” is not supported by any official statements from Pfizer or Microsoft. Neither company has announced any collaboration involving the insertion of microchips into vaccines, nor is there any scientific basis for the idea that a microchip could function in the way described—namely, to reduce COVID-19 symptoms. Vaccine ingredients are subject to rigorous regulatory review, and the addition of any such component would require transparent disclosure and approval by health authorities.

Furthermore, the technical feasibility of embedding a functioning microchip in a vaccine dose, particularly one that could interface with biological systems to reduce symptoms, does not exist with current technology. Microchips require power sources and physical space not compatible with injection through a standard vaccination needle, and no current vaccine contains any electronic device.

In conclusion, the claim that Pfizer has announced an updated COVID-19 vaccine containing a Microsoft chip designed to reduce symptoms is entirely false. It appears to be a continuation of widely debunked conspiracy theories that have circulated since the start of the pandemic. Consumers are encouraged to rely on information from official health organizations and credible news sources, and to approach sensational claims on social media with skepticism. Pfizer’s updated vaccines continue to be based on mRNA or protein subunit technology, with no evidence of any microchip or electronic component involvement.

A social media post has recently gained traction, claiming that “Pfizer documents confirm that vaccinated people put unvaccinated people at risk.” This statement has alarmed many and contributed to ongoing debates and misinformation about COVID-19 vaccines. To evaluate this claim, it is important to examine the origins of this assertion, the content of Pfizer’s documents, and the current scientific understanding of COVID-19 vaccine safety and transmission.

The claim appears to stem from a misinterpretation of clinical trial documents released by Pfizer during the development of its COVID-19 vaccine. In 2021, some social media users referenced sections of a Pfizer clinical trial protocol discussing the monitoring of “environmental exposure” to the vaccine during the trial. This language was intended for researchers to track accidental exposure to the vaccine or its components during the study, such as cases where a researcher might inadvertently come into contact with the vaccine solution or when a pregnant woman might be exposed in a laboratory setting. The document outlined how such rare incidents should be reported, as is standard practice in clinical trials to ensure the safety of both participants and those around them.

Some users, however, interpreted these routine safety protocols as evidence that vaccinated individuals could shed vaccine components or spike proteins, thereby posing a risk to unvaccinated individuals. This interpretation is not supported by scientific evidence or the intent of the trial protocols. COVID-19 vaccines, including the Pfizer mRNA vaccine, do not contain live virus and cannot cause a vaccinated individual to shed virus particles. mRNA from the vaccine is quickly broken down in the body, and the spike protein it produces is not contagious; it is simply a harmless protein used to train the immune system.

There is no evidence to suggest that vaccinated people shed harmful substances that could endanger unvaccinated people. On the contrary, the primary risk of COVID-19 transmission remains the virus itself, which spreads from person to person through respiratory droplets. Vaccinated individuals are less likely to become severely ill and, in many cases, are also less likely to transmit the virus to others if they become infected.

Claims that vaccinated people pose unique risks to the unvaccinated are not supported by data from vaccine trials, real-world studies, or regulatory reviews. Instead, vaccination has been shown to reduce the burden of COVID-19 at the population level, protecting both the individual and those around them by decreasing the likelihood of viral spread.

In summary, the assertion that “Pfizer documents confirm that vaccinated people put unvaccinated people at risk” is a misreading of standard clinical trial safety procedures and does not reflect the scientific consensus or the intent of the documents. The available evidence indicates that COVID-19 vaccines are safe and do not cause vaccinated individuals to pose a risk to the unvaccinated.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that chlorine dioxide is "non-toxic" and is used to clean and disinfect human donor blood, purportedly as documented by a patent. This assertion has generated significant attention and concern, particularly given ongoing misinformation about chlorine dioxide’s safety and uses in medicine. This article examines these claims in detail, providing context, background, and a thorough fact-checking analysis.

**Understanding Chlorine Dioxide**

Chlorine dioxide is a chemical compound primarily used as an industrial bleaching agent and disinfectant. Its most common applications include water treatment, food sanitation, and surface disinfection. Chlorine dioxide is known for its strong oxidizing properties, which make it effective at destroying bacteria, viruses, and some parasites. However, its safety profile is distinctly different from many household disinfectants or food-grade antimicrobials.

**Medical and Regulatory Perspective**

Medical authorities, including national and international health agencies, have consistently cautioned against the ingestion, injection, or inappropriate use of chlorine dioxide in or on the human body. Chlorine dioxide is not approved as a therapeutic agent for any medical condition, and its use in humans outside of controlled, specific industrial or laboratory contexts is considered unsafe. Exposure to chlorine dioxide, especially at high concentrations, can cause serious side effects such as irritation of the respiratory tract, coughing, difficulty breathing, nausea, vomiting, and, in severe cases, damage to organs.

**Examining the Patent Claim**

The social media post references an unspecified patent as evidence that chlorine dioxide is used to “clean and disinfect human donor blood.” It is true that patents sometimes exist describing a wide range of potential applications for chemicals, including theoretical uses in medical procedures. However, the existence of a patent does not equate to regulatory approval, clinical adoption, or real-world safety. Patents are granted for inventions and ideas, not for proven, safe, or effective medical treatments.

In the context of blood donation and transfusion, rigorous protocols are in place to ensure the safety and sterility of blood products. Approved methods for disinfection and pathogen inactivation in blood do not include chlorine dioxide as a standard or accepted practice. Instead, methods such as pathogen reduction technologies using other agents or ultraviolet light are utilized, all of which have undergone extensive scientific evaluation for both efficacy and safety.

**Is Chlorine Dioxide Non-Toxic?**

The assertion that chlorine dioxide is “non-toxic” is misleading. While it may be safe at very low concentrations for certain applications, such as water disinfection, higher concentrations or direct exposure can be hazardous. Regulatory agencies explicitly warn against its use in unapproved contexts, especially those involving internal use in humans. Reports of adverse effects, including serious poisoning and hospitalization, have occurred when people have ingested or injected chlorine dioxide, often as a result of misinformation.

**Conclusion**

The claim that chlorine dioxide is non-toxic and is used to disinfect human donor blood is inaccurate and misleading. While chlorine dioxide has legitimate uses as a disinfectant in industrial and water treatment settings, it is not a recognized or approved agent for cleaning or disinfecting human blood, nor is it non-toxic in the context implied by the social media post. Individuals should rely on evidence-based medical practices and be wary of unsubstantiated medical claims circulating online.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that “Vaccination is a scientific and medical error because it is creating SARS-CoV-2 variants.” This assertion has circulated widely since the rollout of COVID-19 vaccines, fueling concerns and confusion about the role of vaccines in the evolution of the coronavirus. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine how viruses mutate, the influence of vaccination on viral evolution, and what current scientific understanding tells us.

Viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, naturally mutate over time. Each time the virus replicates, errors can occur in its genetic material, leading to the emergence of new variants. Most of these mutations have little to no effect, but some may change the virus’s properties, such as its transmissibility or ability to evade immune responses. These mutations and the resulting variants are a normal part of the viral life cycle and are not unique to SARS-CoV-2.

The core of the social media claim suggests that vaccination itself is the driving force behind the creation of new variants. However, scientific evidence indicates that the primary driver of new variants is the uncontrolled spread of the virus in unvaccinated populations. When the virus infects large numbers of people, it has more opportunities to replicate and mutate, increasing the likelihood of variants arising. Vaccination helps reduce the number of infections, thus lowering the overall chances for the virus to mutate.

A related but distinct concept is “vaccine-driven evolution,” where selective pressure from immunity—whether from vaccination or prior infection—could favor variants able to partially evade immune protection. This process is not unique to vaccines and is a feature of the ongoing battle between pathogens and immune systems. Importantly, the benefits of vaccination—reducing severe disease, hospitalizations, and deaths—far outweigh the potential risk of selecting for immune-evasive variants. In fact, widespread vaccination has proven to be one of the most effective tools for controlling the pandemic and limiting the emergence of new variants by decreasing viral transmission.

It is also worth noting that some of the most concerning SARS-CoV-2 variants, such as the Delta and Omicron variants, emerged before large-scale vaccination campaigns were underway. This timeline contradicts the claim that vaccination is the primary cause of new variants.

In summary, the claim that vaccination is a scientific and medical error because it creates SARS-CoV-2 variants is not supported by current scientific understanding. Vaccines are not the main source of viral mutations; rather, uncontrolled viral spread provides the conditions for variants to arise. Vaccination remains a critical tool in reducing the spread of COVID-19 and, by extension, limiting the opportunities for new variants to develop. Misinformation about vaccines and variants can undermine public health efforts and prolong the pandemic. It is essential to rely on evidence-based guidance and the consensus of the scientific and medical communities when evaluating such claims.

Последња социјална мрежа порука тврди да „Вакцинација је научна и медицинска грешка јер је омогућавала постизање варијанти СARS-CoV-2“. Ово тврђење је широм дистрибуције вакцина против ковида-19, узроковало је брину и несазнање о улоги вакцина у еволуцији коронавируса. Да бисмо проценили тачност овог тврђења, важно је проучити како вируси мутирају, улогу вакцинације у вирусној еволуцији и шта савремена научна знања кажу о томе.

Вируси, укључујући и СARS-CoV-2, природно мутирају током времена. Сваки пут када се вирус репликује, могуће је да се појаве грешке у његовом генетском материјалу, што доводи до појаве нових варијанти. Већина ових мутација има мало или није уопште утицаја, али неке могу да промене својства вируса, као што су његова преносљивост или способност да избегне имунолошка одговора. Ове мутације и резултатни варијанти су природна део вирусног животног циклуса и не су специфичне за СARS-CoV-2.

Кључни део социјалне мреже тврђења предлаже да је сама вакцинација главни извор постизања нових варијанти. Међутим, научни докази указују да је главни узрок нових варијанти не контролисана преносљивост вируса у популацијама које нису вакцинисане. Када вирус инфекцију већег броја особа, има више могућности за репликацију и мутацију, што повећава вероватноћу појаве варијанти. Вакцинација помаже да се смањи број инфекција, што смањује општу могућност мутације вируса.

Повезано, али одвојено појмове је „вакцински еволуција“, где изабирни притисак имунитета – било од вакцинације или претходног инфекције – може да фаворизује варијанте које могу да делimiчно избегну имунитет. Ова процес није специфичан за вакцине, и је карактеристичан за непрекидао борбу између патогена и имунолошког система. Важно је да су користи вакцинације – смањење тежих обољења, болница и смртности – значајно већи од потенцијалног ризика од избора имунитет-евасивних варијанти. Наравно, широка вакцинација је доказала да је једна од најефикаснијих метода за контролисање пандемије и ограничавање појаве нових варијанти, смањујући пренос вируса.

Са овим је важно имати у виду да су неке од најзаштетнијих варијанти СARS-CoV-2, као што су Делта и Омикрон, појавиле се пре широког увода вакцинације. Ова време линија супротставља тврђењу да је вакцинација главни извор нових варијанти.

У закључку, тврђење да је вакцинација научна и медицинска грешка јер изазива варијанте СARS-CoV-2 не подржава савремено научно знање. Вакцине нису главни извор вирусних мутација; уместо тога, не контролисана преносљивост вируса пружа услове за појаву варијанти. Вакцинација остаје критични инструмент за смањење преноса ковида-19 и, пошто је, ограничавање могућности за развој нових варијанти. Неправилна информација о вакцина и варијантама може да оштети напоре јавног здравља и продужи пандемију. Важно је да се оваква тврђења процени на основу доказа и консензуса научне и медицинске заједнице.

Las vacunas reducen la transmisión, limitando oportunidades para mutaciones, y variantes como Delta y Omicron surgieron antes de su implementación masiva. A recent social media post claims that Sweden has discontinued the use of PCR (polymerase chain reaction) tests as a diagnostic tool for COVID-19. This statement has circulated widely and raised concerns about Sweden’s approach to managing the pandemic. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to consider the context of Sweden’s COVID-19 response, the role of PCR testing, and any official changes in policy.

Since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in early 2020, PCR testing has been considered the gold standard for detecting active SARS-CoV-2 infections. These tests are highly sensitive and can identify the presence of viral genetic material even in individuals with low viral loads. Most countries, including Sweden, have relied heavily on PCR tests to confirm cases, inform public health decisions, and track the spread of the virus.

The claim that Sweden has discontinued PCR testing for COVID-19 appears to stem from a misinterpretation of official guidance and changes in testing strategy announced by Swedish health authorities. In early 2022, as much of the population became vaccinated and the Omicron variant surged, Sweden—like several other European countries—adjusted its testing protocols. Swedish health agencies announced that PCR tests would be prioritized for certain groups, such as healthcare workers and vulnerable populations, rather than being offered broadly to the general public. This shift was largely due to high vaccination rates, widespread mild cases, and the strain on testing resources.

However, this policy change does not equate to a complete discontinuation of PCR testing as a diagnostic method for COVID-19. Instead, Sweden reduced the scale and scope of PCR testing, focusing resources where they were most needed. The Swedish Public Health Agency clarified that PCR tests remained available for individuals at higher risk, in healthcare settings, and in situations where a confirmed diagnosis was required for treatment or infection control. Rapid antigen tests and clinical assessments also became more prominent, reflecting a move toward a more targeted testing strategy as the pandemic evolved.

It is also important to note that the decision to scale back widespread PCR testing was not unique to Sweden. Many countries made similar adjustments as the public health landscape changed, balancing the need for surveillance with practical considerations like testing capacity and the prevalence of milder cases.

In summary, the social media post stating that Sweden has discontinued the use of PCRs as a diagnostic test for COVID-19 is misleading. While Sweden has scaled back mass PCR testing and shifted toward targeted use, PCR tests remain an important diagnostic tool for COVID-19 in specific contexts. The change reflects an evolving public health response, not a total abandonment of PCR testing for COVID-19 diagnosis.

article_content:
A recent social media post has gained traction, claiming that a peer-reviewed study published in the highly respected medical journal "The Lancet" confirms vaccine efficacy is not 95% as originally claimed by vaccine manufacturers, but is instead only around 1%. This assertion raises significant concerns about the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines and the reliability of published data. Here, we examine the accuracy of the claim, provide relevant background, and analyze the data referenced.

**Background and Context**

COVID-19 vaccines, such as those developed by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, were widely reported in late 2020 and early 2021 to have efficacy rates of approximately 95%. These figures refer to “relative risk reduction” (RRR) observed in large clinical trials. RRR compares how much the risk of disease is reduced in the vaccinated group compared to the unvaccinated group.

However, some critics have pointed to another metric, “absolute risk reduction” (ARR), which measures the difference in the event rate between the vaccinated and unvaccinated groups. In the original clinical trials, the ARR was much lower—often around 1% or less—because the actual risk of contracting COVID-19 during the trials was relatively small.

**Examining the Claim**

The post claims that a peer-reviewed Lancet study “confirms” vaccine efficacy is about 1%, not 95%. While it is true that some studies published in The Lancet, as well as other medical journals, have discussed both RRR and ARR, the portrayal of these figures is often misunderstood or misrepresented in social media debates.

The 95% efficacy figure is based on relative risk reduction. For instance, if 1% of the placebo group gets infected compared to 0.05% of the vaccinated group, the vaccine reduces the relative risk by about 95%. Absolute risk reduction, in this scenario, would be the difference between those two rates—0.95%—which is the figure referenced by critics.

Some commentaries and letters in The Lancet have indeed pointed out the low ARR numbers, highlighting the importance of communicating both relative and absolute risks to the public for transparency. However, these discussions do not dispute the high relative efficacy of the vaccines in reducing the risk of symptomatic COVID-19. They also do not claim that the “true” efficacy is only 1%; rather, they emphasize that ARR provides additional context, especially in populations with low incidence of disease.

**Fact-Checking Analysis**

The core claim in the post is misleading. While The Lancet and other journals have published articles discussing both RRR and ARR, no peer-reviewed study in The Lancet or elsewhere has “confirmed” that vaccine efficacy is only 1%. Instead, the 95% figure refers to the reduction in risk among participants in clinical trials, and this is the standard measure used in vaccine studies. The approximately 1% figure refers to the absolute risk reduction, which is not a measure of the vaccine’s direct biological effect, but rather reflects the baseline risk in the population studied.

**Conclusion**

The social media post misrepresents the scientific findings and conflates two different statistical measures—relative and absolute risk reductions. COVID-19 vaccine efficacy as measured in clinical trials remains high, with relative risk reductions of around 95% for mRNA vaccines. Absolute risk reduction is a different, context-dependent metric and does not reflect the vaccine’s overall effectiveness in real-world settings. No study in The Lancet has “confirmed” the claim that vaccine efficacy is only 1%.

A widely shared social media post claims that vaccines inject a “metallic solution” into the body that can be tracked by “antennae,” and further asserts that the proteins produced by the vaccine “can destroy the producing cell.” These statements have contributed to ongoing fears and misinformation about vaccine safety and the technology behind modern vaccines, particularly those developed for COVID-19. In this article, we examine the scientific accuracy of these claims and provide context for better understanding.

The first claim is that vaccines inoculate a metallic solution into the body. Vaccines, whether traditional or messenger RNA (mRNA)-based, do not contain “metallic solutions.” Traditional vaccines typically include inactivated viruses or bacterial proteins, water, stabilizers, and sometimes adjuvants such as aluminum salts. These aluminum compounds are used in small, safe amounts to enhance the immune response, not to create a “metallic solution.” The quantity of aluminum in vaccines is far below the amount people routinely encounter through food, water, and air. In the case of mRNA vaccines like those for COVID-19, the main components are the mRNA itself and lipid nanoparticles, which help deliver the genetic material into cells. There are no metals or substances that would create a “metallic solution.”

The post further alleges that this supposed metallic solution can be tracked by “antennae.” This refers to a persistent conspiracy theory suggesting that vaccines contain microchips or components that can be tracked remotely using radio frequency identification (RFID) or similar technologies. No scientific evidence supports this claim. Vaccine ingredients are thoroughly disclosed and monitored by regulatory agencies, and there is no mechanism or technology currently available that would allow tracking of individuals via vaccine ingredients using “antennae” or any other device. The idea of such tracking is not supported by any credible research or health authority.

The second part of the post suggests that the proteins produced by the vaccine can destroy the producing cell. This claim appears to reference the way mRNA vaccines work: the mRNA instructs cells to make a viral protein, which then triggers an immune response. Once the protein is made, the mRNA is broken down and does not remain in the body. The spike protein or other proteins produced are harmless fragments that cannot cause cellular destruction. The immune response targets the viral protein, not the host cell. While very rare side effects can occur with any medical intervention, the overwhelming scientific consensus is that vaccine-produced proteins do not destroy the cells that create them.

In summary, the claims that vaccines inject a metallic solution that can be tracked, and that vaccine-induced proteins destroy the producing cell, are not supported by scientific evidence. Vaccine safety is closely monitored, and the ingredients are rigorously tested and verified. Spreading such misinformation can undermine public trust in vaccines, which remain a critical tool for preventing disease and protecting public health.

A recent social media post claims that vaccines contain graphene, described as a superconductor with magnetic activity. This assertion has generated confusion and concern among some members of the public. Here, we examine the accuracy of these claims by analyzing the composition of vaccines, the properties of graphene, and the scientific consensus on this topic.

To begin with, vaccines are rigorously regulated medical products developed to stimulate the immune system and protect against infectious diseases. Their ingredients are carefully selected and publicly disclosed, typically including weakened or inactivated forms of pathogens, adjuvants to enhance immune response, stabilizers, and preservatives. Since the rollout of COVID-19 vaccines, claims have circulated online alleging the presence of exotic or harmful substances, including graphene.

Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice. It has unique properties: it is exceptionally strong, conducts electricity, and is nearly transparent. However, calling graphene a "superconductor" is factually incorrect. Superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity with zero resistance at very low temperatures. Graphene, while an excellent conductor, does not exhibit superconductivity under normal conditions. Some laboratory experiments have induced superconducting states in engineered graphene structures at extremely low temperatures, but this is not a property of standard graphene.

The claim that graphene has "magnetic activity" also misrepresents the scientific understanding of this material. Pure graphene is not inherently magnetic. Certain modifications or defects can introduce magnetic properties, but these are not present in the standard form of graphene used in research or potential applications.

As for the alleged presence of graphene in vaccines, comprehensive ingredient lists for approved vaccines, including those for COVID-19, do not mention graphene or any graphene-derived material. Regulatory agencies such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency require detailed disclosure and rigorous safety testing of all components in vaccines. To date, there is no credible evidence to support the claim that graphene is an ingredient in any vaccine currently in use.

The origins of this claim appear to stem from misinterpretations or deliberate distortions of scientific studies. In some cases, lab-based research on the potential biomedical uses of graphene, such as in drug delivery or biosensing, has been misconstrued and amplified on social media as evidence that graphene is already present in vaccines. These research efforts are experimental, and none have resulted in the incorporation of graphene into approved vaccines.

In summary, the assertion that vaccines contain graphene is not supported by evidence. Furthermore, the characterization of graphene as a "superconductor with magnetic activity" is scientifically inaccurate. Vaccines remain one of the most scrutinized and transparent medical products available, and their ingredients are well-documented. The spread of misinformation about vaccine contents can undermine public confidence and should be addressed with accurate scientific communication.

ग्राफ़ेन एक कार्बन अणुओं के एक लेयर है जो द्वि-आयामी मधुमक्खी रूप के लैटिस में व्यवस्थित होता है। यह विशेष गुणों के साथ है: यह बहुत मजबूत होता है, विद्युत का चालन करता है और लगभग पारदर्शी होता है। हालांकि, ग्राफ़ेन को "अत्याधुनिक चालक" कहना तथ्यात्मक रूप से गलत है। अत्याधुनिक चालक वे सामग्रियां होती हैं जो बहुत कम तापमान पर विद्युत का शून्य प्रतिरोध के साथ चालन कर सकती हैं। ग्राफ़ेन, एक अद्वितीय चालक होता है, लेकिन सामान्य परिस्थितियों में अत्याधुनिक चालकता नहीं दिखाता है। कुछ प्रयोगशाला प्रयोगों में विशिष्ट ग्राफ़ेन संरचनाओं में बहुत कम तापमान पर अत्याधुनिक चालक अवस्था प्रेरित की गई है, लेकिन यह सामान्य ग्राफ़ेन की गुणों के बारे में नहीं है।

ग्राफ़ेन के "चुंबकीय गतिविधि" के दावे भी इस सामग्री के वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन के बारे में गलत व्याख्या करते हैं। शुद्ध ग्राफ़ेन आत्मस्वाभाविक रूप से चुंबकीय नहीं होता है। कुछ संशोधन या दोष चुंबकीय गुणों को प्रस्तुत कर सकते हैं, लेकिन इन गुणों के अभाव में ग्राफ़ेन के सामान्य रूप में शोध या संभावित अनुप्रयोग में उपयोग किया जाता है।

वैक्सीन में ग्राफ़ेन के उपस्थिति के दावे के बारे में, स्वीकृत वैक्सीन के घटक सूची, जिसमें कोविड-19 के वैक्सीन भी शामिल हैं, ग्राफ़ेन या कोई ग्राफ़ेन उत्पादित सामग्री का उल्लेख नहीं करती है। अमेरिकी खाद्य एवं औषधि प्राधिकरण और यूरोपीय औषधि प्राधिकरण जैसे नियामक एजेंसियां वैक्सीन के सभी घटकों के विस्तृत घोषणा और गंभीर सुरक्षा परीक्षण की आवश्यकता होती है। अब तक, कोई विश्वसनीय आधार नहीं है जो कि वर्तमान में उपयोग में लाए गए वैक्सीन में ग्राफ़ेन के घटक के दावे को समर्थन करता है।

इस दावे के मूल के बारे में लगता है कि वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन की गलत व्याख्या या निश्चित रूप से विकृति के कारण है। कुछ मामलों में, ग्राफ़ेन के बायोमेडिकल उपयोग के संभावित अनुप्रयोग, जैसे दवा वितरण या जैविक संवेदन के लिए प्रयोगशाला अध्ययन, सामाजिक मीडिया पर गलत तरीके से समझा और बढ़ा दिया गया है, जिसके कारण ग्राफ़ेन वैक्सीन में उपस्थित है के रूप में आधार बनाया गया है। ये अनुसंधान अनुभागीय हैं और कोई भी अनुसंधान वैक्सीन में ग्राफ़ेन के उपयोग के रूप में विकसित नहीं किया गया है।

संक्षेप में, वैक्सीन में ग्राफ़ेन के उपस्थिति के दावे के आधार के बिना रहते हैं। इसके अलावा, ग्राफ़ेन के "अत्याधुनिक चालक चुंबकीय गतिविधि" के वर्णन वैज्ञानिक रूप से गलत है। वैक्सीन विश्व के सबसे जांच किये गए और स्पष्ट चिकित्सा उत्पादों में से एक हैं और इनके घटक अच्छी तरह से दस्तावेजीकृत हैं। वैक्सीन के घटकों के बारे में गलत जानकारी के फैलाव लोगों के भरोसा को कम कर सकते हैं और इसके विरुद्ध वैज्ञानिक रूप से सही जानकारी के फैलाव के लिए जिम्मेदारी रखनी चाहिए।

A claim circulating on social media asserts that PCR test swabs contain magnetic "nanoparticles" capable of attracting magnets and metal objects to the skin. This assertion has fueled concerns about the safety and composition of COVID-19 testing, particularly as PCR (polymerase chain reaction) tests have become a primary method for diagnosing COVID-19 infection around the world. Here, we examine the scientific validity of this claim and provide context to assess its accuracy.

PCR tests are designed to detect genetic material from the SARS-CoV-2 virus. The process typically involves inserting a sterile swab into the nasal passage or throat to collect a sample. The swabs used in these tests are generally composed of materials such as nylon, polyester, or flocked fibers attached to a plastic shaft. The collected sample is then processed in a laboratory, where the viral genetic material can be detected and amplified if present.

The claim that the swabs contain magnetic nanoparticles suggests the intentional inclusion of microscopic particles that could respond to magnets or make the skin exhibit magnetic properties. In scientific and medical practice, nanoparticles—extremely small particles measured in nanometers—are sometimes used in specialized diagnostic or therapeutic procedures, such as targeted drug delivery or certain imaging techniques. However, the standard PCR swab test is a simple collection tool and does not require or utilize nanoparticles for sample collection or analysis.

No credible evidence supports the assertion that PCR swabs contain any form of magnetic or metallic nanoparticles. Manufacturing standards for medical devices, including swabs, are tightly regulated to ensure patient safety and prevent contamination. The introduction of extraneous or potentially harmful substances, such as unidentified nanoparticles, would violate these standards and prompt investigation by regulatory authorities. Furthermore, the physical sensation of magnetism—objects sticking to the skin due to magnetic attraction—requires the presence of ferromagnetic materials in sufficient quantity, which would be easily detectable and is not consistent with the composition or design of PCR swabs.

Reports of magnets or metal objects sticking to skin after COVID-19 testing or vaccination have appeared in various social media posts and videos. However, scientific analysis has demonstrated that such effects are typically due to residue, moisture, natural skin oils, or static electricity, rather than the presence of magnetic or metallic particles. These effects are not unique to individuals who have undergone testing or vaccination, and they can be replicated under normal conditions with everyday objects.

In summary, the claim that PCR test swabs contain magnetic nanoparticles is not supported by scientific evidence or regulatory documentation. The materials used in PCR swabs are non-magnetic and non-metallic, and there is no mechanism by which they could impart magnetic properties to the skin. The continued spread of such misinformation can undermine public trust in essential medical testing and public health initiatives. It is important to rely on verified information and the guidance of qualified health authorities regarding the safety and composition of medical devices.

社交媒体上流传着一种说法，称PCR检测拭子含有磁性“纳米颗粒”，能够吸引磁铁或金属物体附着在皮肤上。这一说法引发了人们对新冠病毒检测安全性和成分的担忧，尤其是在全球范围内，PCR（聚合酶链反应）测试已成为诊断新冠病毒感染的主要方法。本文将探讨这一说法的科学依据，并提供背景信息以评估其准确性。

PCR检测旨在检测SARS-CoV-2病毒的遗传物质。通常，该过程包括将无菌拭子插入鼻腔或喉咙以采集样本。这些检测中使用的拭子通常由尼龙、聚酯或刷毛纤维等材料制成，这些材料固定在塑料杆上。采集的样本随后在实验室中进行处理，如果存在病毒遗传物质，就可以检测并放大其信号。

声称拭子含有磁性纳米颗粒，意味着其中故意添加了能够对磁铁产生反应或使皮肤呈现磁性特性的微观粒子。在科学和医疗实践中，纳米颗粒——以纳米为单位测量的极小颗粒——有时会被用于特定的诊断或治疗程序，例如靶向药物输送或某些成像技术。然而，标准的PCR拭子检测是一种简单的采集工具，其采样或分析过程并不需要或使用纳米颗粒。

目前没有任何可信的证据支持PCR拭子含有任何形式的磁性或金属纳米颗粒的说法。医疗设备，包括拭子的制造标准，都受到严格监管，以确保患者安全并防止污染。引入未知的、可能有害的物质，如未识别的纳米颗粒，将违反这些标准，并可能引发监管机构的调查。此外，磁性现象——物体因磁性吸引力而附着在皮肤上——需要存在足够数量的铁磁性材料，这种材料通常易于检测，而与PCR拭子的成分和设计并不一致。

社交媒体上出现了关于在进行新冠检测或接种疫苗后磁铁或金属物体粘附在皮肤上的报告。然而，科学分析表明，这种现象通常是由残留物、水分、天然皮肤油脂或静电引起的，而非磁性或金属颗粒的存在。这些现象并不局限于接受检测或接种疫苗的人群，且在正常情况下，日常物品也能产生类似效果。

总而言之，PCR检测拭子含有磁性纳米颗粒的说法缺乏科学证据或监管文件的支持。PCR拭子所用材料为非磁性且非金属材料，没有机制使其赋予皮肤磁性特征。此类误导性信息的持续传播可能损害公众对重要医疗检测和公共卫生举措的信任。因此，应依靠经过验证的信息和合格卫生机构关于医疗设备安全性和成分的指导。

A social media post claims that the Japanese Red Cross refuses blood donations from people injected with coronavirus vaccines. This assertion has circulated widely, raising concerns about vaccine safety and blood donation policies in Japan. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is necessary to examine the Japanese Red Cross’s official guidelines, the scientific understanding of COVID-19 vaccines, and the broader context of blood donation eligibility.

First, it is important to understand the procedures governing blood donation in Japan. The Japanese Red Cross Society (JRCS) is the principal organization responsible for collecting and managing blood donations in the country. Like other national blood services, the JRCS sets eligibility criteria to ensure both donor and recipient safety. These criteria are periodically updated based on new medical evidence and guidance from health authorities.

In the context of COVID-19, several types of vaccines have been utilized in Japan, including mRNA vaccines (such as Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) and viral vector vaccines (such as AstraZeneca). Globally, the introduction of COVID-19 vaccines prompted blood services to review and often update their donation guidelines. The main concerns for deferral after vaccination generally relate to monitoring for any immediate adverse effects in donors, not to the vaccine’s contents or safety for blood recipients.

The claim that the Japanese Red Cross refuses all blood donations from vaccinated individuals is inaccurate. Official statements and guidelines from the Japanese Red Cross confirm that people who have received COVID-19 vaccines are not automatically barred from donating blood. Instead, there is a short waiting period after vaccination, which is a standard precaution for many types of vaccines. For example, individuals who have received an inactivated or mRNA vaccine are typically eligible to donate blood after a waiting period of 48 hours, provided they are feeling well and have not experienced significant side effects. Those who have received live attenuated vaccines (which do not include the major COVID-19 vaccines used in Japan) may be subject to a longer deferral period.

These deferral periods are not unique to COVID-19 vaccines; they are standard practice for a range of vaccinations and are intended to ensure the donor’s well-being and to monitor for any acute adverse reactions. The Red Cross in many countries, including Japan, has emphasized that blood from vaccinated donors is safe and that there is no evidence to suggest that COVID-19 vaccines contaminate or otherwise compromise the safety of donated blood.

In summary, the assertion that the Japanese Red Cross refuses blood donations from people injected with coronavirus vaccines is false. The organization permits blood donation from vaccinated individuals after a short waiting period, consistent with international practices and medical guidelines. Such misinformation may contribute to unwarranted fear and vaccine hesitancy, as well as unnecessary concerns over blood supply safety. It is always advisable to consult official sources or contact the Japanese Red Cross directly for the most current and accurate information about blood donation eligibility.

Ein Beitrag auf sozialen Medien behauptet, dass das Japanische Rote Kreuz Blutspenden von Personen ablehnt, die mit Impfstoffen gegen das Coronavirus injiziert wurden. Diese Behauptung ist weit verbreitet und verursacht Sorgen hinsichtlich der Sicherheit der Impfstoffe und der Blutspendepolitik in Japan. Um die Genauigkeit dieser Behauptung zu bewerten, ist es notwendig, die offiziellen Richtlinien des Japanischen Rote Kreuzes (JRCS), das wissenschaftliche Verständnis der Impfstoffe gegen das Coronavirus und den breiteren Kontext der Blutspendegültigkeit zu untersuchen.

Zunächst ist es wichtig, die Verfahren zur Blutspende in Japan zu verstehen. Die Japanische Rote Kreuz-Gesellschaft (JRCS) ist die zentrale Organisation, die für die Sammlung und Verwaltung von Blutspenden im Land verantwortlich ist. Wie andere nationale Blutdienste legt die JRCS auch Gültigkeitskriterien fest, um sowohl die Sicherheit der Spender als auch der Empfänger zu gewährleisten. Diese Kriterien werden regelmäßig anhand neuer medizinischer Erkenntnisse und Empfehlungen der Gesundheitsbehörden aktualisiert.

Im Kontext der COVID-19-Pandemie wurden in Japan mehrere Arten von Impfstoffen eingesetzt, darunter mRNA-Impfstoffe (z. B. von Pfizer-BioNTech und Moderna) und virusbasierte Vektorimpfstoffe (z. B. von AstraZeneca). Global führte die Einführung von Impfstoffen gegen das Coronavirus zu einer Überprüfung und oft auch zu einer Aktualisierung der Spendenrichtlinien durch Blutdienste. Die Hauptbedenken nach der Impfung beziehen sich in der Regel auf die Beobachtung möglicher unmittelbarer Nebenwirkungen bei Spendern, nicht auf den Inhalt der Impfstoffe oder deren Sicherheit für Blutempfänger.

Die Behauptung, dass das Japanische Rote Kreuz alle Blutspenden von geimpften Personen ablehnt, ist unrichtig. Offizielle Stellungnahmen und Richtlinien des Japanischen Rote Kreuzes bestätigen, dass Personen, die einen Impfstoff gegen das Coronavirus erhalten haben, nicht automatisch von der Blutspende ausgeschlossen sind. Stattdessen gibt es einen kurzen Wartezeitraum nach der Impfung, der bei vielen Impfstofftypen Standardvorsichtsmaßnahme ist. Beispielsweise sind Personen, die eine inaktivierte oder mRNA-Impfung erhalten haben, typischerweise nach einer Wartezeit von 48 Stunden für die Blutspende berechtigt, sofern sie sich gut fühlen und keine erheblichen Nebenwirkungen verspüren. Personen, die lebend attenuierte Impfstoffe (die nicht unter die wichtigsten in Japan verwendeten Impfstoffe gegen das Coronavirus fallen) erhalten haben, können möglicherweise einem längeren Wartezeitraum unterliegen.

Diese Wartezeitperioden sind nicht nur für Impfstoffe gegen das Coronavirus typisch; sie sind Standardpraxis bei einer Vielzahl von Impfungen und dienen dazu, die Wohlfahrt des Spenders zu gewährleisten und mögliche akute Nebenwirkungen zu überwachen. Das Rote Kreuz in vielen Ländern, einschließlich Japan, betont, dass Blut von geimpften Spendern sicher ist und es keine Beweise gibt, die darauf hindeuten, dass Impfstoffe gegen das Coronavirus die Sicherheit von gespendetem Blut beeinträchtigen oder kontaminieren.

Zusammengefasst ist die Behauptung, dass das Japanische Rote Kreuz Blutspenden von Personen ablehnt, die mit Impfstoffen gegen das Coronavirus injiziert wurden, falsch. Die Organisation gestattet Blutspenden von geimpften Personen nach einem kurzen Wartezeitraum, was mit internationalen Praktiken und medizinischen Richtlinien übereinstimmt. Solche Fehlinformationen können unverdiente Angst und Impfscheu sowie unverhältnismäßige Bedenken hinsichtlich der Sicherheit der Blutversorgung hervorrufen. Es ist immer ratsam, offizielle Quellen zu konsultieren oder direkt mit dem Japanischen Rote Kreuz Kontakt aufzunehmen, um aktuelle und genaue Informationen zur Blutspendegültigkeit zu erhalten.

In recent years, social media has become a breeding ground for conspiracy theories surrounding vaccines and public health measures. One claim that has gained traction involves Pierre Gilbert, a Canadian preacher, alleged to have predicted that people would be forced to take vaccines containing liquid crystals, which would be used to control individuals. This article examines the context of Gilbert's statements, the veracity of the claim, and the scientific plausibility of the alleged prediction.

Pierre Gilbert is best known for a sermon he delivered in 1995, during which he warned of potential future attempts to control humanity through medical interventions. The claim circulating on social media states that Gilbert foresaw a time when vaccines would be deliberately used to introduce liquid crystals into the human body, allowing for mass control of individuals, possibly even through electromagnetic waves. Some versions of the claim suggest that Gilbert's prediction directly references COVID-19 vaccines.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to review what Gilbert actually said during his sermon. In the original statement, Gilbert spoke about "biological destruction" being imposed on populations through contaminated blood, food, and vaccines. He mentioned the possibility of "liquid crystals" being injected into individuals, which could allow for mind control through electromagnetic waves. However, Gilbert did not provide scientific evidence for these assertions, nor did he specify any particular vaccine or time frame for this alleged phenomenon.

The claim that Gilbert predicted forced vaccination for control through liquid crystals is therefore partly accurate in that he made statements alluding to such a scenario. However, there is no evidence to suggest that his predictions were based on scientific fact or that they were intended as anything other than speculative warnings. Furthermore, the suggestion that vaccines currently in use, including the COVID-19 vaccines, contain liquid crystals for the purpose of controlling individuals is not supported by scientific research or medical data.

Modern vaccines, including those for COVID-19, are formulated using thoroughly tested ingredients designed to stimulate the immune system and provide protection against infectious diseases. The concept of "liquid crystals" in the context of vaccines is not recognized by medical science. Liquid crystals are materials with properties between those of conventional liquids and solid crystals and are commonly used in display technology, not in pharmaceuticals. There is no credible evidence that any vaccine contains such materials, nor that they could be used to exert control over individuals.

In conclusion, while Pierre Gilbert did make speculative remarks in 1995 about vaccines and liquid crystals, the claim that he accurately predicted forced vaccination for mass control is misleading. His statements lack scientific foundation and have been misappropriated in the context of recent public health measures. There is no factual basis to the notion that current vaccines contain liquid crystals or are used for mind control. The spread of such misinformation can contribute to vaccine hesitancy and undermine public health efforts. It is crucial to consult reliable sources and scientific authorities when evaluating claims about vaccines and their ingredients.

为评估这一说法的准确性，有必要回顾吉尔伯特在布道中实际说过的话。在原始声明中，吉尔伯特提到“生物性毁灭”将通过污染的血液、食物和疫苗施加于人口。他提到有可能将“液态晶体”注入个人体内，从而通过电磁波实现对人的思想控制。然而，吉尔伯特并未提供这些说法的科学证据，也未明确提及任何特定的疫苗或该现象的时间框架。

因此，吉尔伯特曾预言通过液态晶体实施强制接种以实现控制的说法在某种程度上是准确的，因为他确实发表了涉及此类情景的言论。然而，没有任何证据表明他的预言基于科学事实，或者其意图是任何其他形式的推测性警告。此外，目前使用的疫苗，包括新冠疫苗，不含用于控制个人的液态晶体的说法，缺乏科学研究或医学数据的支持。

现代疫苗，包括新冠疫苗，都是使用经过彻底测试的成分制成，旨在刺激免疫系统以保护人体免受传染病侵害。在疫苗语境中，“液态晶体”这一概念在医学科学中并不被认可。液态晶体是一种介于传统液体和固体晶体之间的材料，常用于显示技术，而不是制药领域。目前没有任何可信证据表明任何疫苗含有此类材料，也没有证据表明它们可用于控制个人。

总而言之，尽管皮埃尔·吉尔伯特在1995年曾对疫苗和液态晶体做出过推测性评论，但称他准确预言了通过强制接种实现大规模控制的说法是误导性的。他的言论缺乏科学基础，并且在近期公共卫生措施的背景下被误用。目前没有任何事实依据表明现有疫苗含有液态晶体或被用于思想控制。此类错误信息的传播可能加剧疫苗犹豫，削弱公共卫生努力。在评估有关疫苗及其成分的主张时，咨询可靠来源和科学权威至关重要。

A widely shared social media post claims that a team comprised of more than 1,000 lawyers and over 10,000 medical experts has initiated legal proceedings against the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the World Health Organization (WHO), and the Davos Group (commonly understood as the World Economic Forum) for crimes against humanity, with the trial purportedly beginning on July 3, 2021. This claim has garnered significant attention, raising questions about its authenticity and prompting a need for thorough fact-checking.

To assess the accuracy of the post, it is important to consider the background and context of the organizations mentioned, as well as the logistics and public record of legal proceedings of such magnitude. The CDC and WHO are prominent public health agencies whose roles have been central during the COVID-19 pandemic. The Davos Group, or the World Economic Forum, is an international organization that brings together political, business, and other leaders annually in Davos, Switzerland, to discuss global issues. Accusations against these bodies alleging crimes against humanity are serious and would likely result in substantial media coverage and official documentation.

First, the claim that over 1,000 lawyers and 10,000 medical experts have formed a coalition to file a lawsuit is extraordinary. Large legal actions, such as class-action lawsuits or international tribunals, are typically announced through press releases, court filings, and are covered by multiple news outlets. A trial of this scale against major international organizations would be a historic event, expected to appear in major newspapers, television broadcasts, and official court records.

Upon reviewing publicly available information from July 2021 and the months leading up to and following that date, there is no credible evidence of such a trial commencing against the CDC, WHO, or the Davos Group. No court records exist to substantiate the claim of a legal proceeding of this scope, nor is there documentation of the formation of a coalition of 1,000 lawyers and 10,000 medical experts pursuing these charges. While there have been critics of the pandemic response and some legal challenges in various jurisdictions, these have been limited in scope and have not involved the alleged numbers of professionals or the specific charges of crimes against humanity.

The origin of the claim appears to be rooted in misinformation campaigns that proliferated during the COVID-19 pandemic. Some online personalities and conspiracy theorists have made similar assertions, often referencing supposed legal actions that have never materialized or have been misrepresented. In reality, international crimes such as “crimes against humanity” are typically adjudicated by bodies like the International Criminal Court, which follows well-established procedures and public disclosure norms. No official proceedings against the WHO, CDC, or World Economic Forum have been documented by such institutions.

In conclusion, there is no factual basis for the claim that a massive team of lawyers and medical experts initiated legal proceedings against the CDC, WHO, and the Davos Group for crimes against humanity, nor that a trial began on July 3, 2021. The absence of supporting evidence, official records, and media coverage strongly indicates that this social media post is inaccurate and misleading. As with any significant allegation, it is essential to rely on verified sources and official documentation before accepting such claims as fact.

The claim that "Spike or S proteins produced by mRNA injections against COVID-19 are toxic" has circulated widely on social media, sparking concern and debate about the safety of COVID-19 vaccines. To assess the accuracy of this statement, it is important to understand what spike proteins are, how mRNA vaccines work, and what scientific evidence says about their safety.

Background and Context

COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, such as those developed by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, use messenger RNA technology to instruct human cells to produce a version of the spike protein found on the surface of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. This spike protein is not the virus itself; it is a harmless piece used to train the immune system to recognize and respond to SARS-CoV-2. Once the spike protein is made, the immune system identifies it as foreign and builds antibodies and immune cells that can fight the virus if the person is exposed in the future.

The Claim

The core claim in the social media post is that these spike proteins, produced as a result of the vaccine, are "toxic." This suggests that the proteins themselves cause harm to the body, rather than acting as a harmless trigger for the immune response.

Fact-Checking Analysis

The scientific consensus is that the spike protein produced by mRNA vaccines is not toxic in the context of vaccination. The spike protein generated is similar to the one found on the virus but is produced in a controlled manner and in much smaller quantities. Once produced, the protein is displayed on the surface of cells, prompting the immune system to recognize and remember it. Importantly, the mRNA in the vaccines is rapidly broken down and does not persist in the body, and the spike protein itself is temporary.

Most people experience mild and temporary side effects following vaccination, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, headache, or fever, which are signs of the immune system at work. Serious adverse events are exceedingly rare. There is no evidence showing that the spike protein produced by the vaccine accumulates in the body, causes toxicity, or leads to widespread harm.

It is true that the spike protein is involved in the process by which the actual virus infects cells and causes disease. However, the key difference is that in COVID-19 infection, the virus rapidly multiplies and produces large amounts of spike protein, which can contribute to disease symptoms. In contrast, mRNA vaccines result in limited and short-lived production of spike protein, sufficient only to trigger immune memory.

Conclusion

The assertion that the spike protein produced by mRNA COVID-19 vaccines is toxic is not supported by current scientific evidence. While the spike protein is essential for triggering an immune response, there is no indication that it is harmful when produced by the body following vaccination. COVID-19 mRNA vaccines have undergone rigorous testing and monitoring, and their safety profile has been established through millions of administered doses worldwide. Social media claims suggesting spike protein toxicity may contribute to vaccine hesitancy but do not reflect the scientific understanding of vaccine safety.

Käyttöönotto, että "mRNA-injektioita vastaan COVID-19:ta kohtaan tuottamat Spike- tai S-proteiinit ovat toksisia", on levinnyt laajasti sosiaalisen median keskuudessa ja aiheuttanut huolia ja keskustelua COVID-19-vakioinnin turvallisuudesta. Täsmällisen arvioinnin tarpeen tarkastella tämän väitteen oikeutusta on tärkeää ymmärtää, mitä Spike-proteiinit ovat, miten mRNA-vakioinnit toimivat ja mikä tieteellinen tieto vahvistaa niiden turvallisuutta.

Taustatietoa ja yleistä

COVID-19 mRNA-vakioinnit, kuten Pfizer-BioNTechin ja Modernan kehittämät, käyttävät viestintä-RNA-teknologiaa, joka ohjaa ihmisen soluja tuottamaan SARS-CoV-2-viruksen pinnalla olevan Spike-proteiinin versio. Tämä Spike-proteiini ei ole itse virusta, vaan se on turhautunut osa, jota käytetään kehittämään immuunijärjestelmän tunnistamista ja vastaamista SARS-CoV-2-virus kohtaan. Kun Spike-proteiini on valmistettu, immuunijärjestelmä tunnistaa sen ulkoiseksi ja rakentaa vastaavia vasta-aineita ja immuunisoluja, jotka voivat vastustaa virusta, jos henkilö altistuu virukselle tulevaisuudessa.

Väite

Sosiaalisen median viestissä keskeinen väite on, että nämä Spike-proteiinit, jotka tuotetaan vakioinnin myötä, ovat "toksisia". Tämä viittaa siihen, että proteiinit itse aiheuttavat vahinkoa kehossa, eikä toimi vain turhautuneena käynnistimenä immuunivasteen synnyttämiseksi.

Todellisuuden tarkastelu

Tieteellinen yhteisö ei tukea väitettä siitä, että mRNA-vakioinnin tuottama Spike-proteiini olisi toksinen vakioinnin yhteydessä. Tuotettu Spike-proteiini on samanlainen kuin viruksen pinnalla oleva, mutta se tuotetaan hallitusti ja paljon pienemmissä määrissä. Kun proteiini on valmistettu, se näkyy solujen pinnalla, mikä herättää immuunijärjestelmän tunnistamisen ja muistin. Tärkeää on huomata, että vakioinnissa käytettävä RNA hajoaa nopeasti ja ei säily yksilössä, ja itse Spike-proteiini on väliaikainen.

Suurin osa ihmisistä kokee vakioinnin jälkeen lievän ja tilapäisen oireiden, kuten injektion paikalla olevan kipun, väsymisen, päänsärkyn tai kuumetta, jotka ovat merkkejä immuunijärjestelmän toiminnasta. vakioinnin vakavat haitalliset tapahtumat ovat hyvin harvinaisia. Ei ole osoitettu, että vakioinnin tuottama Spike-proteiini kertyisi kehoon, aiheuttaisi toksisuutta tai johtaisi laajaa vahinkoa.

On totta, että Spike-proteiini on osa prosessia, jolla todellinen virus altistaa soluja ja aiheuttaa sairautta. Tärkein ero on siinä, että COVID-19-infektiolla virus kertaalleen kaksinkertaistuu ja tuottaa suuren määrän Spike-proteiinia, joka voi osaltaan vaikuttaa sairauksen oireisiin. Vastoin tätä, mRNA-vakioinnit johtavat rajoitettuun ja lyhytaikaiseen Spike-proteiinin tuotantoon, joka on tarpeeksi vahvaa, jotta immuunijärjestelmä muistaa virusta.

Johtopäätös

Väite siitä, että mRNA-COVID-19-vakioinnit tuottavat toksisen Spike-proteiinin, ei ole tieteellisesti perusteltua. Vaikka Spike-proteiini on keskeinen immuunivasteen käynnistämiseen, ei ole osoitettu, että se aiheuttaa vahinkoa, kun se tuotetaan kehossa vakioinnin jälkeen. COVID-19 mRNA-vakioinnit ovat läpitetty rutiininomaisesti testaukseen ja valvontaan, ja niiden turvallisuus on perustettu miljoonien vakioinnin jälkeen maailmanlaajuisesti. Sosiaalisen median väitteet, jotka ehdottavat Spike-proteiinin toksisuutta, voivat lisätä vakioinnin vastustusta, mutta ne eivät vastaa tieteellistä ymmärrystä vakioinnin turvallisuudesta.

La seguridad de las vacunas ha sido validada mediante millones de dosis y seguimiento riguroso, con efectos secundarios leves y raras reacciones graves.

A social media post has been circulating, claiming that a confidential document shows Moderna already had a COVID-19 vaccine before the pandemic began. This assertion has sparked significant debate and concern online, with some users suggesting that it demonstrates foreknowledge or premeditation regarding the global outbreak of COVID-19. To assess the validity of this claim, it is necessary to examine the timeline of events, the science behind vaccine development, and the content and context of the purported “confidential document.”

The core claim suggests that Moderna, a biotechnology company, had fully developed a COVID-19 vaccine prior to the official recognition of the pandemic, which the World Health Organization declared in March 2020. According to public records, the novel coronavirus, later named SARS-CoV-2, was first identified in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. The virus’s genetic sequence was published by Chinese scientists in early January 2020, which allowed researchers and pharmaceutical companies worldwide to begin developing targeted vaccines.

Moderna was among the first companies to initiate vaccine development after the genetic code became available. Their approach utilized messenger RNA (mRNA) technology, a platform they had been researching for years in the context of other viruses, such as Zika and MERS (a related coronavirus). The mRNA platform allows for rapid adaptation to new viral threats, but the COVID-19 vaccine, specifically targeting SARS-CoV-2, was not in existence before the identification and sequencing of the virus responsible for COVID-19.

The “confidential document” referenced in the social media post appears to have originated from misinterpretations or selective readings of patent filings, research papers, or regulatory submissions. In some instances, documents have been cited that discuss generic coronavirus vaccine platforms or materials exchanged between companies prior to 2020. These documents do not demonstrate the existence of a finished COVID-19 vaccine before the pandemic; rather, they reflect ongoing research into mRNA-based technologies and generic coronavirus targets, which are a family of viruses including those that cause the common cold, MERS, and SARS.

It is standard practice for pharmaceutical companies to explore broad vaccine platforms for various pathogens, including coronaviruses, as part of pandemic preparedness. When the specific sequence of SARS-CoV-2 became available, Moderna and other companies rapidly adapted their existing platforms to target the new virus. The clinical development, testing, and regulatory review processes for the COVID-19 vaccines began after January 2020 and were subject to public and regulatory scrutiny.

In summary, the claim that Moderna possessed a COVID-19 vaccine before the pandemic lacks supporting evidence. Available information indicates that while Moderna had been developing mRNA technology and working on vaccines for related viruses, their COVID-19 vaccine was designed and produced only after the SARS-CoV-2 genome was released in 2020. The assertion based on a “confidential document” misrepresents the nature of vaccine research and the timelines involved. Claims suggesting otherwise are not substantiated by the documented sequence of scientific and regulatory events leading to the development of COVID-19 vaccines.

Lời khẳng định cốt lõi cho rằng Moderna, một công ty công nghệ sinh học, đã phát triển đầy đủ vaccine ngừa COVID-19 trước khi chính thức công nhận đại dịch, được Tổ chức Y tế Thế giới tuyên bố vào tháng 3 năm 2020. Phương pháp tiếp cận của họ sử dụng công nghệ ARN thông tin (mRNA), một nền tảng mà họ đã nghiên cứu trong nhiều năm trong bối cảnh các virus khác, như Zika và MERS (một loại virus corona liên quan). Việc các công ty dược phẩm nghiên cứu các nền tảng vaccine chung cho nhiều loại vi sinh vật, bao gồm virus corona, là một thực tiễn thông thường trong việc chuẩn bị cho đại dịch. Khi mã gen cụ thể của SARS-CoV-2 trở nên khả dụng, Moderna và các công ty khác đã nhanh chóng điều chỉnh nền tảng hiện có để nhắm mục tiêu virus mới này. Tóm lại, lời khẳng định rằng Moderna sở hữu vaccine ngừa COVID-19 trước đại dịch không có bằng chứng hỗ trợ. Thông tin có sẵn cho thấy, mặc dù Moderna đã nghiên cứu công nghệ mRNA và phát triển vaccine cho các virus liên quan, vaccine ngừa COVID-19 của họ chỉ được thiết kế và sản xuất sau khi mã gen SARS-CoV-2 được công bố vào năm 2020. Lời khẳng định dựa trên "tài liệu mật" này đã làm sai lệch bản chất của nghiên cứu vaccine và các thời gian biểu liên quan. Các khẳng định cho rằng điều ngược lại là đúng không được chứng minh bằng các sự kiện khoa học và quản lý được ghi lại dẫn đến việc phát triển các vaccine ngừa COVID-19.
